## Script Summary
In this script, we determine which covariates to include in our differential analysis (per cancer type in each omics layer)
using various criteria: 

For all Projects:
  - Only run differential analysis if there are at least 50 samples for that omics layer

  - Include gender if we have at least 5 of each gender and one gender isn't more than 90% of the samples

  - Include race if we have at least two races with ≥5 samples each (excluding races with <5 samples)

  - Include grade (`histological_grade`) if there are at least two grade categories with ≥5 samples each, and at least 75% of samples have grade information. 

  - Include HPV status for HNSC only (see this github issue for details why  https://github.com/orgs/montilab/projects/2?pane=issue&itemId=84862253&issue=montilab%7Cpancancer-aging%7C16)

  For BRCA: Include tumor molecular subtype (PAM50)

We also: 
  - Creates tables for determined covariates per cancer type, across omics layers

  - Creates table showing discrepancies for determined covariates between omics layers of a given cancer type

  - Saves determined covariates for each omics layer as tables in RDS files 

Future considerations:
  - Include tumor subtype for other cancer types?? (22 projects have info)

## Load in FILTERED SummarizedExperiments
These paths should lead to the directories containing analysis ready SummarizedExperiment objects
in the form of RDS files. Its important these SummarizedExperiments are fully processed so we can accurately determine 
which projects we have enough samples for (50) and determine the appropriate
covariates. 

Note the # of samples reported here may not line up with the # of samples in the harmonized meta data script. There are additonal samples in the clinical information which are not found
in the downloaded TCGA data (not sure why, could be addtional tumor types or samples not part of the official TCGA study)

For now, we use the "processed_data/all" objects for the 4 omics layer with these objects generated (miRNA, RPPA, RNAseq, DNA methylation)

For SCNA and mutation, we utilize the raw SummarizedExperiment objects with the harmonized meta data added (not yet a focus of our analyses). 


```{r Data locations}
#Load in all RDS files of a directory
file_list_METHYL <- list.files(
  path = file.path(TCGA,"methylation/processed_data/all"), 
  pattern = "*.rds", full.names = TRUE)

file_list_RPPA <- list.files(
  path = file.path(TCGA,"RPPA/processed_data/all"),
  pattern = "*.rds", full.names = TRUE)

# as specified by Pranav Narnur
file_list_SCNA <- list.files(
  path = file.path(TCGA, "scna/GISTIC/processed_data") , 
  pattern = "*segment.rds", full.names = TRUE)

file_list_RNASEQ <- list.files(
  path = file.path(TCGA,"RNAseq/processed_data/all"), 
  pattern = "*.rds", full.names = TRUE)

file_list_MIRNA <- list.files(
  path = file.path(TCGA,"miR/processed_data/all"),
  pattern = "*.rds", full.names = TRUE)

file_list_MUTATION <- list.files(
  path = file.path(TCGA,"mutation/processed_data/all"),
  pattern = "*.rds", full.names = TRUE)
```


## Determine Covariates
This code is designed to process SummarizedExperiment objects stored as RDS files for our 6 omics data types (e.g., METHYL, RPPA). It dynamically determines which covariates to include for differential analysis based on predefined criteria. Specifically:

1. Gender is included as a covariate if there are at least 5 samples for each gender, and no single gender comprises more than 90% of the samples.

2. Race is considered if there are at least two different racial categories, each with more than 5 samples. The "not reported" category is excluded from this analysis.

3. Grade (histological_grade) is included if there are at least two grade categories with ≥5 samples each, and atleast 75% of samples have grade information. 

4. HPV status is included for HNSC only. 

5. For the BRCA project, the tumor molecular subtype (PAM50) is included.

6. Tumor Purity is included if at least 75% of samples have available purity information

The output is a data frame for each omics type, detailing the cancer type, the number of samples, and whether each covariate (gender, race, subtype, HPV status, grade, etc) meets the criteria for inclusion.

For race, it includes which races we have ample sample size for (>5 samples).
```{r Data Process Function}
process_rds_file <- function(file_path, omics_type) {
  # Load in file
  se <- readRDS(file_path)
  
  # Get file name
  file_name <- basename(file_path)
  
  # Finds cancer type in file name, adds TCGA if necessary
  matches <- regmatches(file_name, regexpr("(TCGA-)?[A-Z]+", file_name))
  cancer_type <- ifelse(length(matches) > 0, gsub("TCGA-", "", matches), NA)
  cancer_type <- ifelse(!is.na(cancer_type), paste0("TCGA-", cancer_type), cancer_type)
  
  # Get number of samples
  num_samples <- ncol(se)
  
  # Define mandatory and optional metadata columns
  mandatory_columns <- c("gender", "race", "purity")
  optional_columns <- c("subtype_selected", "HPV.status", "histological_grade")
  
  # Check for existence of mandatory metadata columns in colData
  missing_mandatory <- mandatory_columns[!mandatory_columns %in% colnames(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se))]
  
  if (length(missing_mandatory) > 0) {
    stop(paste("Meta data is not up to date!! Missing mandatory columns:", paste(missing_mandatory, collapse=", ")))
  }
  
  # Check for existence of optional metadata columns
  available_optional <- optional_columns[optional_columns %in% colnames(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se))]
  
  
  # Initialize covariates to include as FALSE; they will be updated based on criteria
  include_purity <- FALSE 
  include_gender <- FALSE
  races_included <- ""  # Store race information
  include_subtype <- FALSE
  include_HPV_status <- FALSE
  include_grade <- FALSE
  grades_included <- ""  # Store grade information
  include_race <- FALSE
  
  if (num_samples >= 1) { 
    # Gender criteria
    genders <- table(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$gender)
    min_gender <- min(genders)
    max_gender_percent <- max(genders) / sum(genders) * 100
    if (min_gender >= 5 && max_gender_percent <= 90) {
      include_gender <- TRUE
    }
    
    # Race criteria, excluding "not reported", checking for at least two races with >5 samples
    races <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$race
    valid_races <- races[races != "not reported" & !is.na(races)]
    race_counts <- table(valid_races)
    valid_race_names <- names(race_counts[race_counts >= 5])
    if (length(valid_race_names) >= 2) {
      include_race <- TRUE
      races_included <- paste(valid_race_names, collapse=", ")
    }
    
    #add purity if atleast 75% of samples have it
    purity <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$purity
    non_na_purity <- sum(!is.na(purity))
    if (non_na_purity / num_samples >= 0.75) {
        include_purity <- TRUE
      }
    
    # Tumor subtype for BRCA
    if ("subtype_selected" %in% available_optional && stringr::str_detect(cancer_type, "BRCA")) {
      # Check if there are at least two subtypes with >=5 samples
      subtypes <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$subtype_selected
      subtype_counts <- table(subtypes)
      valid_subtypes <- names(subtype_counts[subtype_counts >= 5])
      if (length(valid_subtypes) >= 2) {
        include_subtype <- TRUE
      }
    }
    
        # Include HPV for head and neck cancer 
    if ("HPV.status" %in% available_optional &&stringr::str_detect(cancer_type, "HNSC")) {
        include_HPV_status <- TRUE
    }
    
    
    # Grade inclusion: at least two grade categories with >=5 samples
    if ("histological_grade" %in% available_optional) {
      #get infor
      grades <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$histological_grade
      
      #get number of grades non-na and distribution
      non_na_grade <- sum(!is.na(grades))
      valid_grades <- grades[!is.na(grades)]
      grade_counts <- table(valid_grades)
      
      #check criteria
      valid_grade_names <- names(grade_counts[grade_counts >= 5])
      
      if (non_na_grade / num_samples >= 0.75 & length(valid_grade_names) >= 2) {
        include_grade <- TRUE
        grades_included <- paste(valid_grade_names, collapse=", ")
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(data.frame(
    cancer_type = cancer_type, 
    omics_type = omics_type,
    num_samples = num_samples,
    include_gender = include_gender,
    include_race = include_race,
    races_included = ifelse(include_race, races_included, NA),
    include_subtype = include_subtype,
    include_HPV_status = include_HPV_status,
    include_grade = include_grade,
    grades_included = ifelse(include_grade, grades_included, NA),
    include_purity = include_purity
  ))
}

# Runs above function on all files in list
process_files <- function(file_list, omics_type) {
  purrr::map_df(file_list, process_rds_file, omics_type = omics_type)
}

# Adds try statement to above function
process_with_try <- function(file_list, omics_type) {
  try({
    results <- process_files(file_list, omics_type)
    return(results)
  }, silent = FALSE)  
}

```

Call the above function on all OMICS types
```{r data process}
results_METHYL <- process_with_try(file_list_METHYL, "METHYL")
results_RPPA <- process_with_try(file_list_RPPA, "RPPA")
results_RNAseq <- process_with_try(file_list_RNASEQ, "RNAseq")
results_miRNA <- process_with_try(file_list_MIRNA, "miRNA")
results_SCNA <- process_with_try(file_list_SCNA, "SCNA")
results_Mutation <- process_with_try(file_list_MUTATION, "Mutation")
```

## Covariate Differences between Omics Layers {.tabset}
Here we show a combined covariate table between our omics types to look for differences
in covariate assignment for the same cancer type across different omics layers.

Note, many of these differences are caused by some cancer projects missing omics layers 
(e.g., TCGA-GBM has only 5 miRNA samples). miRNA in GBM would likely not even be
analyzed given the current 50 sample requirement. 

We also show, for each covariate, identical cancer types that have differences in covariates between omics layers. This issue may or may not be impactful, but is important to
keep in mind during analysis.

```{r}
# Bind all results into one data frame
all_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  results_METHYL, 
  results_RPPA, 
  results_miRNA, 
  results_SCNA, 
  results_RNAseq, 
  results_Mutation, 
  .id = "omics_id"
)

# Transform data to wide format for comparison
wide_results <- all_results %>%
  dplyr::select(cancer_type, omics_type, include_gender, include_race, include_subtype, include_HPV_status, include_grade, include_purity) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = omics_type,
    values_from = c(include_gender, include_race, include_subtype, include_HPV_status, include_grade, include_purity)
  )


reactable::reactable(wide_results)
```

## Number of Samples with Complete Information 
Here we determine how many samples we have available for differential that have complete information for all
dynamically determined covariates for that cancer-omics combination (and available Age).

The number of samples after filtering assumes ALL covariates are included, and also excludes races/grades with insufficient sample information (not part of the races_included/grades_included column). 

```{r}
# Function to filter SummarizedExperiment object based on inclusion criteria
filter_samples_based_on_criteria <- function(file_path, covariate_info) {
  # Load the SummarizedExperiment object
  se <- readRDS(file_path)
  
  # Get file name
  file_name <- basename(file_path)
  
  # Extract cancer type using regex, ensuring it matches the format in covariate_info
  ct <- regmatches(file_name, regexpr("(TCGA-)?[A-Z]+", file_name))
  ct <- ifelse(!grepl("^TCGA-", ct), paste0("TCGA-", ct), ct)
  
  # Find the matching row in covariate_info
  cancer_type_row <- covariate_info[covariate_info$cancer_type == ct, ]
  
  if (nrow(cancer_type_row) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No covariate information found for cancer type:", ct))
    return(data.frame(
      cancer_type = ct,
      omics_type = NA,
      num_samples_before = ncol(se),
      num_samples_after = NA
    ))
  }
  
  # Extract inclusion criteria
  include_gender <- cancer_type_row$include_gender
  include_race <- cancer_type_row$include_race
  include_subtype <- cancer_type_row$include_subtype
  include_HPV_status <- cancer_type_row$include_HPV_status
  include_grade <- cancer_type_row$include_grade
  include_purity <- cancer_type_row$include_purity
  
  races_to_keep <- cancer_type_row$races_included
  grades_to_keep <- cancer_type_row$grades_included
  
  omics_type <- cancer_type_row$omics_type
  
  # Get the number of samples before filtering
  num_samples_before <- ncol(se)
  
  # Initialize a logical vector indicating samples to keep
  keep_samples <- rep(TRUE, num_samples_before)
  
  #first remove missing age
  keep_samples <- keep_samples & !is.na(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$Age)
  
  # Apply filtering based on the inclusion criteria
  if (include_gender) {
    keep_samples <- keep_samples & !is.na(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$gender)
  }
  
  # Apply filtering based on the inclusion criteria
  if (include_purity) {
    keep_samples <- keep_samples & !is.na(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$purity )
  }
  
  if (include_race) {
    races_to_keep_list <- strsplit(as.character(races_to_keep), ",\\s*")[[1]]
    keep_samples <- keep_samples & 
      !is.na(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$race) & 
      SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$race %in% races_to_keep_list
  }
  
  if (include_subtype) {
    keep_samples <- keep_samples & !is.na(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$subtype_selected)
  }
  
  if (include_HPV_status) {
    keep_samples <- keep_samples & !is.na(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$HPV.status)
  }
  
  if (include_grade) {
    grades_to_keep_list <- strsplit(as.character(grades_to_keep), ",\\s*")[[1]]
    keep_samples <- keep_samples & 
      !is.na(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$histological_grade) & 
      SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$histological_grade %in% grades_to_keep_list
  }
  
  # Subset the SummarizedExperiment to keep only the valid samples
  se_filtered <- se[, keep_samples]
  
  # Get the number of samples after filtering
  num_samples_after <- ncol(se_filtered)
  
  return(data.frame(
    cancer_type = ct,
    omics_type = omics_type,
    num_samples_before = num_samples_before,
    num_samples_after = num_samples_after
  ))
}

# Create a function to filter each file in an omics type based on the processed results
filter_all_files_in_omics <- function(file_list, results_df) {
  # Split the results_df into a list of single-row data frames
  results_split <- split(results_df, seq(nrow(results_df)))
  
  # Map over file_list and results_split simultaneously
  purrr::map2_df(file_list, results_split, ~filter_samples_based_on_criteria(.x, .y))
}

# Apply the filtering to each omics type
filtered_results_METHYL <- filter_all_files_in_omics(file_list_METHYL, results_METHYL)
filtered_results_RPPA <- filter_all_files_in_omics(file_list_RPPA, results_RPPA)
filtered_results_RNAseq <- filter_all_files_in_omics(file_list_RNASEQ, results_RNAseq)
filtered_results_miRNA <- filter_all_files_in_omics(file_list_MIRNA, results_miRNA)
filtered_results_SCNA <- filter_all_files_in_omics(file_list_SCNA, results_SCNA)
filtered_results_Mutation <- filter_all_files_in_omics(file_list_MUTATION, results_Mutation)

# Combine the filtered results into a summary table
all_filtered_results_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  filtered_results_METHYL,
  filtered_results_RPPA,
  filtered_results_RNAseq,
  filtered_results_miRNA,
  filtered_results_SCNA,
  filtered_results_Mutation
)

# Display summary table showing number of samples before and after filtering
reactable::reactable(
  all_filtered_results_summary,
  searchable = TRUE,
  resizable = TRUE,
  columns = list(
    cancer_type = reactable::colDef(name = "Cancer Type"),
    omics_type = reactable::colDef(name = "Omics Type"),
    num_samples_before = reactable::colDef(name = "# of Samples Before Filtering"),
    num_samples_after = reactable::colDef(name = "# of Samples After Filtering")
  )
)
```
